segments.text: What you're looking at is called a loss surface. Every point on this surface represents how wrong your model is for a particular combination of parameters.
The higher the point, the worse the model performs. Our goal is to find the lowest point — the minimum.
This dot marks where training begins. Notice it starts high up on the surface — the model is making large errors at this point.
The arrow shows the gradient — the direction of steepest ascent. To reduce loss, we move in exactly the opposite direction.
Think of it like water flowing downhill — it always takes the path of greatest descent.
Watch as the point moves one step downhill. The loss value in the corner drops with each step.
This is one iteration of gradient descent. In practice, training repeats this thousands or millions of times.
